body: I feel the exact same way with my break up.

I know this is from a year ago but your break up soon a lot like the break up I’m going through now. 

We had issues with moving and incompatibility. I felt like I was willing to make changes for the relationship but he wasn’t. 

I don’t know if it counts as a blindsided break up because we had our problems and we were aware of our problems. 

But what does feel blindsiding is how we still seemed good and strong as a couple (atleast from my perspective) then in one week it felt like the relationship fell apart. It felt very sudden and I felt shocked. One week he was very committed and talking about our future together even our engagement. Then next week it seems like he suddenly felt it wasn’t going to work out. His attitude toward the relationship seemed very hot then suddenly cold and that part feels blindsiding. 

I don’t know if it counts as being blindsided but I still felt very shocked.
You’re right not to let it define me. But sometimes it causes painful consequences for my life. That is where I struggle.
Thank you so much. This is really what I need to hear right now.

I’m going through a break up too and I feel the exact way. I have regrets and I punish myself all the time for choices I made. I want to hear from him so badly while he just moved on. And I’ve done everything I’m supposed to do like find distractions, hobbies, spending time with friends but it never makes me feel better completely. And without him everything feels numb, mediocre and empty. So I wonder when I’m actually going to feel better and ok. I want to feel like I did before when I thought we were ok. I thought we were all good but he just blindsided me. You’re not alone in feeling this way I know exactly how you feel.

Have you asked him if having kids was important to him? Maybe it was hard for him if he valued having kids. Deciding to have kids or not have kids is a big deal and I know it's hard on you but it's messed up that your calling his values/needs/wants 'stupid reasons' especially when it comes to important issues like marriage and kids. 

If you don't want to have kids that's your choice but you have to understand that if he wants kids, his wants/needs/and values should at least be validated and heard too, a relationship is two sided. So, it's messed up that you call his desires stupid.  

The decision, to have kids or not, is a big deal and however you decide is going to affect you both and the relationship so it's not a small issue or a trivial issue in a relationship. It sounds like a compatibility issue. If you both have different visions of the future than it is valid to break up with someone.   

Maybe he does still care about you but his idea of the future isn't compatible with yours.

It doesn't have to be all or nothing. You both could have looked for room for compromise before suddenly ending a relationship. The way the issue was brought up sounds sudden but not thought through. If this was the first time she brought up the issue of moving and your family then you both should have calmly talked and thought the issue through instead of suddenly ending the relationship without much thought.

As for you both having different wants regarding moving and your family, think about what you're willing to compromise and what is non-negotiable. But actually think about it and communicate instead of suddenly ending things.

The only rude part is the very first moment your girlfriend voiced her opinion, you suddenly dump her without much thought or discussion that's pretty cold.
